sources.title: GitHub - fortunatetumbleweed-commits/ship_direction · GitHub
sources.snippet: It's correct on all 9 real occluded frames — including t083, which the dataset originally mislabeled (truth210 puts the ship on open water). The part model read 174°; the CNN and the matcher both read ~211°, making the same mistake as the label. That's the cautionary tale: a bad label survives when your models agree with it.

sources.title: GitHub - fortunatetumbleweed-commits/ship_direction
sources.snippet: A U-Net trained to estimate a ship's direction (heading) in an 80×80 top-down game frame — where the ship may be almost entirely hidden behind portraits, village-name text, and minimap markers — and to reconstruct the whole ship at that heading. Heading is 0° = up (north), clockwise.
